Current source-vintage record was captured by the task controller at launch; receipt.json reports inputs_unchanged=true. No substitute sources or downloaded inputs were used.
changes: Retained the accepted fiscal-year clock and separate Table 4 fits. Extended each original fit by five calendar-year labels, pooled with its original observations: FY1974–1988, FY1984–1998, and FY1994–2010. The added periods are FY1984–1988, FY1994–1998, and FY2006–2010, respectively.

Rebuilt historical and added observations together with the accepted SAS construction. Compustat source bounds now reach FY2012 for the maximum t+2 outcome; the current-year sample screen reaches FY2010. The exact monthly/daily GBP-bridge source filter reaches 2013-12-31, while the latest usable Compustat DATADATE is 2013-05-31.

Kept the accepted item mappings, currency conversions, sample screens, ratio caps, OLS terms, no-fixed-effects specification, firm/year clustering, intercept, and Stata/SAS handoff. Added e(sample)-based original/added counts and last-added fiscal year to each selected fit cell; FYEAR remains in the handoff as a fiscal-year label.

Changed the duplicate-assets diagnostic output to fiscal-year aggregates only. The fresh SAS and Stata run succeeded with return code 0 for SAS build and all six assigned fit cells; the controller receipt confirms source inputs were unchanged.
limitations: Scope is the six executed Table 4 persistence regressions only: Panel A h=1 and Panel B h=2 for the three assigned fiscal-year subperiods. The accepted reconstruction did not run the paper's Table 3 logit, Table 5 payout-rank, repurchase, or later regular-payer analyses; those are outside this job's assigned scopes.

The accepted reconstruction is best-effort and already differs from the paper's reported Table 4 Ns and coefficients. The extended estimates continue that same accepted construction and were not tuned to published values. The current table export uses p-values in parentheses, while the paper reports two-way robust standard errors in parentheses.

FUNDA.FIC is labeled Current ISO Country Code – Incorporation; no dated incorporation-history source is available in the authorized catalog. The historic U.S.-incorporation screen therefore uses annual-row FIC and has a timing limitation.

Industry uses valid historical FUNDA.SICH first, then one unique date-valid CCM-linked CRSP MSENAMES.SICCD only when SICH is missing/zero; SICH controls disagreements. The paper does not specify numeric SIC boundaries, so the accepted code uses 6000–6999 for financial and 4900–4999 for utilities. Unresolved and ambiguous classifications remain excluded under that best-effort rule.

Modern Compustat Xpressfeed IDIT is the accepted mapping for legacy item #62 based on the 2007 provider guide. Missing IDIT is not set to zero, and NOPI−NOPIO is not used as a substitute; the paper does not specify a missing-interest policy. The observed-IDIT complete-case restriction can lower N. FUNDA lacks IDIT_DC, so combined-item status cannot be checked row by row.

The accepted sample had two duplicated GVKEY/FYEAR source keys across FY1982–1983 (four rows), all lacking IDIT. The current FY1973–2012 standardized source has five duplicate keys in total, with one new key each in FY2010, FY2011, and FY2012. Current and future earnings retain only unique firm-year periods; duplicate-period lagged assets are retained only if exactly one source row has observed positive AT and a positive own-date USD conversion. The model uses this established tie rule without selecting an ambiguous earnings row.

The historical listing screen uses valid CCM links and date-valid MSENAMES rows, then requires at least one link with share code 10/11 and exchange code 1/2/3. This is the accepted best-effort firm-level interpretation of the paper's NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ criterion.

The accepted GBP-bridge conversion leaves missing/nonpositive FX legs unavailable. Exact current-source checks found complete unique positive monthly and daily matches for standardized annual rows in FY2006–2012; some earlier non-USD source rows lack matched rates and are not imputed. USD remains the accepted identity conversion.
